cosy-lesson.title: Are We Too Obsessed with Perfect-Looking Food?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Symmetrical – made up of exactly similar parts facing each other or around an axis.

p.em: Example: Supermarkets demand symmetrical produce because they look better on display.

cosy-blockquote.p: Asymmetrical – having parts or aspects that are not equal or equivalent; lopsided.

p.em: Example: An asymmetrical tomato tastes exactly the same as its perfectly round counterpart.

cosy-blockquote.p: Anti-waste – actions or campaigns aimed at preventing the discard of usable resources.

p.em: Example: The anti-waste campaign by Intermarché saved hundreds of tons of perfectly good fruits.

cosy-blockquote.p: Calibrate – mark, standardize, or adjust against a precise standard or scale.

p.em: Example: Sorting machines calibrate food sizes so that every potato matches the exact same box.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pristine – in its original condition; unspoiled or clean.

p.em: Example: The supermarket's pristine displays can make shoppers highly critical of minor natural flaws.

cosy-blockquote.p: Superficial ≠ Profound – existing or occurring at or on the surface; shallow ≠ very great, intense, or displaying deep intellectual or emotional insight.

p.em: Example: Rejecting food based on minor scars is a superficial behavior, whereas understanding food waste is a profound realization.

cosy-blockquote.p: Deformed – misshapen or distorted out of its natural shape.

p.em: Example: They renamed deformed vegetables as "ugly" to make them sound charming and lovable.

cosy-blockquote.p: Unrealistic – not representing or showing things as they are in real life.

p.em: Example: Imposing unrealistic standards on farm produce leads to massive ecological waste.

cosy-blockquote.p: Discard – get rid of someone or something as no longer useful or desirable.

p.em: Example: Farms are often forced to discard nearly forty percent of their harvest.

cosy-blockquote.p: Nutritious – efficient as food; containing highly beneficial substances.

p.em: Example: These lumpy carrots are actually more nutritious than the ones grown with heavy chemical fertilizers.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why are we utterly repulsed by minor physical flaws in organic produce, insisting everything be perfectly symmetrical, yet we expect ourselves to accept our partners' psychological imperfections?
★ When was the last time you felt utterly critical of a partner's minor flaw on the first date?

Is a slightly blemished apple perfectly acceptable to you, or does a pristine, untouched skin make you feel that it is more safe and nutritious?
★ What is one personal habit of yours that is perfectly imperfect, yet you refuse to change it?

Why are modern consumers highly sensitive to supermarket aesthetics, while our ancestors celebrated any harvest regardless of its shape?
★ Do you consider yourself highly visual when choosing products, or do you value substance over form?

Are you deeply concerned about the scale of global organic waste, or do you view it simply as an inevitable byproduct of modern logistics?
★ Have you ever felt deeply connected to a social cause, or do you prefer to focus on your immediate personal circle?

Is purchasing 'ugly' produce an exceptionally smart way to reduce anti-waste, or is it merely a trendy moral decoy?
★ What is the most exceptionally creative way you have ever recycled or reused something to avoid waste?

Why has natural, unmodified food become such an elusive luxury in regions like Bretagne?
★ How do you find your calm amidst the elusive peace of a bustling urban center?

Do supermarkets prioritize corporate profits over environmental ethics when they discard tons of edible vegetables simply because they are slightly deformed?
★ How do you prioritize your spending when choosing between cheap convenience and organic, ethical options?

When a company advertises its anti-waste campaigns, do you suspect it's merely a clever pretext to calibrate its public image?
★ Have you ever used an environmental pretext solely to avoid doing something you disliked?

Does the artificial scarcity of perfect produce set an unrealistic standard, making us feel that we are eating something more premium and elite?
★ How do you deal with the psychological sense of scarcity in your own daily routines?

Do you reckon that future generations will look back at our food waste with complete disgust and apathy?
★ Do you reckon you could live a zero-waste lifestyle for a single week?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: - 👑A curated, visually perfect life of surface aesthetics. (Curated Safety) - 🌱An asymmetrical, organic, messy life of raw flaws. (Misshapen Truth)

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: - 👑A curated, visually perfect life of surface aesthetics. (Curated Safety) - 🌱An asymmetrical, organic, messy life of raw flaws. (Misshapen Truth)

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, supermarkets will be legally forced to sell misshapen food, simply because resource scarcity will make visual snobbery utterly unsustainable.
★ Do you think we are highly spoiled by the endless availability of perfect goods?

The Instagram-aesthetic has trained us to reject organic blemishes, creating a dangerous illusion that life must be perfectly curated at all times.
★ Have you ever felt deeply inadequate after comparing your real life with someone's flawless social media feed?

One day, we will look back at our food waste and realize it was merely a protective armor to hide our collective fear of physical decay.
★ Why do we prioritize superficial beauty when it comes to things we simply consume?

True intimacy cannot survive when we screen potential partners on the pretext of minor aesthetic or lifestyle mismatch.
★ Have you ever brushed off a good person solely due to a superficial first impression?

Supermarkets use plastic packaging as a stylized decoy to hide the organic, asymmetrical nature of the food they sell.
★ Do you prefer raw, unpackaged market vegetables, or do you feel safer with standardized, wrapped produce?

In a highly optimized city, finding a space that embraces messy, unstructured growth has become an elusive luxury.
★ Do you feel more at peace in a perfectly manicured French garden or a wild, untamed forest?

To reduce global waste, societies must learn to prioritize environmental survival over immediate consumer comfort.
★ Would you accept a higher tax on non-recyclable packaging, or do you reckon it is the government's job to solve?

Most economists reckon that the smarter our waste management systems become, the less personal responsibility citizens will feel.
★ Do you actively sort your trash, or do you feel a creeping apathy about your personal impact?

Our obsession with food expiration dates is merely a modern superstition that has replaced our natural sensory instincts.
★ Do you trust your nose and taste buds, or do you strictly follow the printed date on the box?

We have built a highly sanitized lifestyle to escape the raw truth of nature, but we have simply ended up with emotional apathy.
★ How do you reconnect with your raw, organic self when you feel completely numb?
